items.title: Bloomberg This Weekend 8/08/2026
items.content: <article>The news doesn’t stop when markets close. Hosts David Gura, Christina Ruffini and Lisa Mateo bring clarity, context and a bit of humor to the weekend’s biggest headlines, LIVE from New York. Joined by Oxford Centre on Migration, Policy & Society Senior Researcher Myriam Cherti, Merrill & Bank of America Head of Market Strategy Joe Quinlan, the New Yorker Staff Writer and Author “Age of Ambition” Evan Osnos and Sportswriter & “LIV and Let Die” Author Alan Shipnuck. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Private Credit Squeezed By Bank Refinancings: Credit Weekly
items.author: Aaron Weinman and Rachel Graf
items.content: <article>Highly-indebted companies are increasingly ditching private credit loans for cheaper capital in the bank loan market, a shift underscoring the stark realities of higher-for-longer interest rates.</article>

items.title: Pointed! Bloomberg's Weekly News Quiz For Risk-Takers
items.content: <article>Pointed offers a strategic twist to the news quiz format, testing not just players’ knowledge of the news but also their confidence in their answers. Join Bloomberg's David Gura, Christina Ruffini and Lisa Mateo as they play and check out the quiz for yourself at Bloomberg.com (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: LIV Golf Tries to Survive Without Saudi Billions
items.content: <article>LIV Golf is seeking fresh investments as it prepares to cut purses and move away from the huge guaranteed payments that helped it lure some of golf’s biggest stars. Author of "LIV or Let Die" Alan Shipnuck is on Bloomberg This Weekend to explain that the league’s future may depend on retaining players including Jon Rahm and Bryson DeChambeau while proving it can attract enough fans and revenue to operate with less financial support from Saudi Arabia. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: China’s AI Push Reshapes Its Economic Future
items.content: <article>New Yorker staff writer Evan Osnos is on Bloomberg This Weekend and says China is taking a practical approach to AI, rapidly deploying the technology in factories and seeking to expand its use across emerging markets rather than focusing primarily on the pursuit of artificial general intelligence. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: US Senate narrowly confirms Todd Blanche as US attorney-general
items.content: <article>Vote follows tense fight that exposed bipartisan concerns about installing an ally of President Donald Trump</article>

items.title: US Munitions Strain Complicates Iran Strategy
items.content: <article>The US remains outside formal negotiations with Iran as Oman and Tehran discuss arrangements for the Strait of Hormuz, leaving the diplomatic path uncertain and raising the possibility of renewed fighting. Joining Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg News White House & National Security Editor Michelle Jamrisko explains to David Gura and Christina Ruffini that strains on US munitions supplies are complicating Washington’s options, with the Pentagon pushing defense contractors to accelerate production while balancing weapons needs across Iran, Ukraine and other potential conflicts. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Hunting Camo Moves From the Woods to Runways
items.content: <article>Hunting camouflage has moved from the woods into mainstream fashion, fueled by demand for vintage workwear and rural American aesthetics. Bloomberg Weekend Senior Features Writer Madison Darbyshire is on Bloomberg This Weekend to explain how the trend has reached streetwear and luxury fashion, where inexpensive hunting gear can inspire pieces costing thousands of dollars and give urban consumers a way to adopt the imagery of traditional masculinity and blue-collar culture. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: University of California Faculty Push to Bring Back SAT and ACT Score Consideration
items.content: <article>Thousands of University of California faculty members are pushing the system to reconsider its test free admissions policy, arguing that SAT and ACT scores could help identify students prepared for college-level work as concerns grow about grade inflation and AI use. Bloomberg News Education Policy Reporter Liam Knox explains to hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that the university has launched a faculty-led review, but opponents argue standardized tests can reinforce socioeconomic disparities, and UC says no change will affect students applying for fall 2027 admission. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: CEO Greg Abel Starts Making His Mark at Berkshire
items.content: <article>Berkshire Hathaway stepped up spending under CEO Greg Abel, repurchasing about $4.5 billion of its shares while deploying billions more into investments. Bloomberg Intelligence and Senior P&C Insurance Equity Analyst Matthew Palazola is on Bloomberg This Weekend explaining to hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that Abel appears more focused on operations and putting Berkshire’s enormous cash reserves to work, marking an early shift from Warren Buffett’s final years at the helm. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: AI Buildout Keeps Quinlan Bullish on US Stocks
items.content: <article>Merrill & Bank of America Head of Market Strategy Joe Quinlan is on Bloomberg This Weekend to give his reaction to the July jobs report. Quinlan explains to hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that the US economy remains resilient despite the weak July jobs data, pointing to continued hiring in construction and health care and investment tied to AI. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: By The Way: Headline You May Have Missed the Week of 8/2
items.content: <article>Sports game streaming, RFK Jr.'s cooking show, $100 hot dogs, and getting into college without applying. Bloomberg News' Lisa Mateo joins David Gura and Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend to share headlines you may have missed from over the week. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Ceuta Migrant Surge Exposes Morocco’s Economic Strain
items.content: <article>More than 70,000 people, mostly Moroccans, crossed into Spain’s North African enclave of Ceuta in a mass migration surge fueled by economic frustration and amplified by social media. Senior Researcher at Oxford University Centre on Migration, Policy & Society Myriam Cherti is on Bloomberg This Weekend to discuss the unusual influx of those looking to cross. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Weak Jobs Data Masked by Falling Unemployment
items.content: <article>The US unexpectedly lost 23,000 jobs in July while unemployment fell to 4.1%, a decline driven by fewer people participating in the labor force rather than stronger employment. Bloomberg News Economics Chief US Economist Anna Wong joins Bloomberg This Weekend and explains to hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that the weak payrolls and persistent downward revisions point to a softer labor market and could reduce pressure on the Fed to raise rates in September. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Fintech That Soared on Trump Sells Core Business for $12 Million

items.content: <article>A virtually unknown fintech that catapulted into the headlines and cracked a $1 billion market value after signing a deal with the Trump family’s crypto platform last year has sold its core business for about $12 million.</article>

items.author: Bloomberg News
items.content: <article>A fire was sparked at Russia’s Ilsky oil refinery in the southern Krasnodar region by Ukrainian drone debris, injuring five people, the regional task force said on Saturday, as Russia and Ukraine exchanged overnight attacks including a large-scale missile barrage on Kyiv.</article>
